title: Implement Splunk HEC audit-export connector (batching, optional ACK, error taxonomy, metrics)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Build the Splunk HEC destination connector for the audit-export worker.

Scope
- Implement Splunk HEC HTTP sender with batching and per-event failure attribution.
- Support optional HEC ACK mode (when customer has HEC acknowledgements enabled).
- Define error handling taxonomy (auth vs throttling vs retryable server vs permanent payload/schema) and map to retry/DLQ behaviors.
- Emit connector-level metrics needed for SLOs and on-call triage.

Background / references
- ADR-0218: Splunk HEC auth + ACK model (Confluence)
- Design spec: audit-export filtering and delivery guarantees (Confluence)

Implementation requirements
1) Batching
- Batch by both (a) max events per request and (b) max request size in bytes.
- Default limits (can be tuned via config):
  - max_batch_events=200
  - max_batch_bytes=900KB (keep under common proxy/body limits)
  - max_single_event_bytes=128KB (larger => classify as permanent failure)
- Serialize as Splunk HEC event payload(s) with consistent metadata:
  - host: "redwood"
  - source: "redwood:audit"
  - sourcetype: "redwood:audit:v1"
  - index: from destination config (required)
  - time: audit event timestamp (seconds)
  - event: full AuditEvent v1 JSON object

2) Auth + transport
- Token-based auth via Authorization: Splunk <token>
- TLS required; support custom CA bundle for Private deployments (config-controlled).
- Respect proxy settings / egress rules (Private).

3) Optional ACK mode
- If destination.ack_enabled=true:
  - Include header X-Splunk-Request-Channel: <uuid> (per worker instance, stable across process lifetime).
  - POST /services/collector/event (or /event/1.0 depending on base URL) and read ackId from response.
  - Poll /services/collector/ack with {"acks":[ackId]} until acked or timeout.
  - ACK poll loop must be bounded:
    - ack_timeout=30s default
    - ack_poll_interval=500ms -> 2s (backoff)
  - Only checkpoint/commit queue offsets after ACK indicates delivered.
- If ack_enabled=false:
  - Treat HTTP 200 with success code as delivered; checkpoint immediately.

4) Error taxonomy and behavior
- Permanent (do not retry; send to DLQ with reason):
  - 400 invalid payload / parsing errors
  - 404 wrong endpoint (config error)
  - event too large (max_single_event_bytes)
  - schema validation failure pre-send
- Auth/config (pause destination; surface clear error; require customer action):
  - 401/403 invalid token or permissions
  - TLS handshake failures due to bad cert / hostname mismatch
- Retryable:
  - 408/429, network timeouts, connection resets
  - 5xx from Splunk HEC
  - ACK polling: if initial send succeeded but ACK polling times out, treat as retryable with at-least-once semantics (may duplicate).
- Throttling handling:
  - Honor Retry-After where present.
  - Exponential backoff with jitter, max backoff cap (e.g., 60s) coordinated with worker retry policy.

5) Observability / metrics
- Counters:
  - audit_export_splunk_requests_total{status_class}
  - audit_export_splunk_events_sent_total
  - audit_export_splunk_events_failed_total{reason}
  - audit_export_splunk_retries_total{reason}
  - audit_export_splunk_dlq_writes_total{reason}
- Histograms:
  - audit_export_splunk_request_latency_ms
  - audit_export_splunk_batch_events
  - audit_export_splunk_batch_bytes
  - audit_export_splunk_ack_latency_ms (only if ack_enabled)
- Gauges:
  - audit_export_splunk_inflight_requests

Acceptance criteria
- Connector can deliver audit events to Splunk Cloud and on-prem HEC endpoints with correct sourcetype/index mapping.
- ACK mode blocks checkpointing until acked and is bounded to avoid worker deadlock.
- Retry/permanent classification matches taxonomy above and is visible via destination health fields.
- Integration tests cover: 401/403, 429 with Retry-After, 5xx burst, partial-batch failures, ACK happy path, ACK timeout.

Out of scope
- HEC raw endpoint support (keep to event endpoint for beta)
- Customer-specific field mapping beyond AuditEvent v1 schema
comments: 2025-02-06 (Diego Santos): Drafted connector interface + config shape. Defaulting to HEC /services/collector/event. Need to confirm base URL expectations for Splunk Cloud vs on-prem; will accept full URL in destination config and append endpoint path only if not provided.

2025-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure we do not log HEC token under any circumstances. Redact Authorization header and destination config secrets in structured logs. Also add explicit error string for 401/403 that tells customer to rotate token / validate HEC input permissions.

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): For on-call, we need clear separation of retryable vs permanent so we don’t page on customer misconfig forever. Suggest: auth/config errors should transition destination state to Degraded and stop retrying until config change (or a cooldown).

2025-02-11 (Diego Santos): Implemented error classifier:
- auth_config: 401/403, TLS verification failure
- throttled: 429/503 with Retry-After
- retryable: 408, 5xx, network
- permanent: 400/404, payload too large
Wired to worker to request pause-on-auth via destination health update hook (pending ENG-13928 API fields).

2025-02-13 (Allison Grant): Metrics naming looks good. Please add ack latency histogram and also export response body parsing errors as permanent failure reason=invalid_response so we can distinguish from schema invalid. Also include status_class label as 2xx/4xx/5xx rather than raw status to keep cardinality down.

2025-02-17 (Diego Santos): ACK mode implemented behind destination.ack_enabled. Using a stable request channel UUID per worker process; ack polling bounded with timeout=30s and backoff 0.5s->2s. If ACK times out, we retry send with same event payload (at-least-once; duplicates possible). Added explicit docs comment in code and surfaced as health.last_error includes "ack_timeout".

2025-02-19 (Leila Farouk): Added integration test cases using mock HEC server:
- 401/403 -> no retry, state=degraded
- 429 Retry-After -> respects delay (assert next attempt >= header)
- 5xx burst -> retries with exponential backoff
- ACK success -> checkpoint after ack
- ACK timeout -> retries and emits ack_timeout metric

2025-02-21 (Diego Santos): Open question: payload format. We’re sending {"time": <sec>, "host": "redwood", "source": "redwood:audit", "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:v1", "index": <cfg>, "event": <AuditEvent>} per Splunk event endpoint. Batch is newline-delimited JSON events in a single POST. This matches common HEC usage and avoids wrapping arrays (Splunk accepts both, but NDJSON is more standard).

2025-02-24 (Ethan Park): Approved approach. Please ensure max batch bytes enforced post-serialization (UTF-8 bytes), not pre-estimate by event count. Also add max_single_event_bytes check prior to enqueue if feasible; otherwise enforce in connector and DLQ with reason=event_too_large.

2025-02-26 (Diego Santos): Merged PR in audit-log-exporter repo: pr_0141 "Splunk HEC connector with optional ACK support". Includes batching, classifiers, metrics, and tests. Follow-up filed in ENG-13928 to ensure health surfaces ack_timeout distinctly in Console.

2025-03-01 (Rafael Mendes): Verified dashboards in staging show request rate, 429s, and ack latency. Runbook note added: if Splunk returns intermittent 5xx, pause destination if backlog grows; duplicates expected on retry per at-least-once semantics.
